Description: The 443NN range (e.g. 44300, 44301, etc.) refers to the SAP Internet Communication Manager (ICM) interfaces configured for HTTPS transport. These interfaces provide secure access to HTTP-based SAP services and are often found in production landscapes behind SAP Web Dispatcher or external TLS-aware load balancers. This is the TLS-secured sibling of the 80NN range.
Deployment Context: The 443NN ports are typically mapped to NetWeaver ABAP or dual-stack systems. These ports are often exposed internally or externally to serve SAP WebGUI, Fiori Launchpad, Web Dynpro apps, or integration APIs like OData and SOAP. Depending on system configuration, they may be accessed directly or through an intermediary like SAP Web Dispatcher performing SSL termination.
Functional Capabilities: 443NN provides HTTPS access to SAP content normally seen over 80NN. This includes rich user interfaces such as the SAP GUI for HTML (`/sap/bc/gui/sap/its/webgui`), Fiori-based launchpads (`/sap/bc/ui5_ui5/ui2/ushell`), Business Server Pages (`/sap/bc/bsp/*`), Web Dynpro apps, and machine-consumable endpoints like `/sap/opu/odata`. It also facilitates login portals and service trees rooted in SICF.
Authentication Mechanisms: These ports often surface authentication flows such as form-based login UIs, SAML2 identity federation portals, and X.509/TLS client certificate negotiation. Many customers use these entrypoints to enforce centralized SSO and secure federation across corporate landscapes.
Stack Characteristics: 443NN ports reflect the underlying application stack. On ABAP systems, the ICM handles requests and routes them via the SICF tree to services like WebGUI, NWBC, and custom BSP apps. On Java systems, the servlet container (e.g., SAP NetWeaver Application Server Java) may also respond, depending on integration. Some ports support hybrid services (ABAP + Java content).
Assessment Goals: This module will eventually fingerprint the stack type, enumerate accessible URIs, analyze TLS configuration, extract headers and cookies, and validate whether applications or login surfaces are exposed insecurely. The goal is to identify weak TLS policies, exposed service endpoints, and misconfigured login flows.
Security Implications: 443NN ports are often left exposed without tight restrictions. Insecure login UIs, legacy SAML flows, open OData endpoints, and verbose stack banners have been observed in real-world setups. If accessible from the internet or untrusted networks, these ports represent a major attack surface for both auth bypass and post-auth exploits.
Assessment Notes: An open 443NN port often signals a fully operational and externally accessible SAP Web Interface — backed by NetWeaver ABAP, Java, or both. This is the path through which many admin portals, app interfaces, and third-party integrations operate. A misstep here can expose core application logic and authentication surfaces to attackers.
